name: positive-cross-file-revision-detected
scenario: Agent extracts FY1947 Army expenditures from an older bulletin without checking the newer bulletin for revised figures.
task: Two Treasury Bulletin files are provided: one published April 1948, one published December 1952. Both contain Table 3 with military expenditure data by fiscal year. The question asks for FY1947 Army net expenditures. The older file shows FY1947 Army = 7,425; the newer file shows FY1947 Army = 6,911 (restated). Both files' footnotes confirm Air Force is included within Army for FY1947.
source_data: File A (April 1948): Table 3, FY1947 Army = 7,425. Footnote: 'Air Force expenditures included under Army for 1947.' File B (December 1952): Table 3, FY1947 Army = 6,911. Footnote: 'Air Force expenditures included under Army for fiscal year 1947.' Both files are listed as source files for the task.
expected_behavior: Skill activates before agent finalizes the value. Agent cross-checks File B, discovers the revision, confirms consistent reporting structure via footnotes, and selects 6,911 from the later publication as the authoritative figure.
expected_intermediate: Identifies target data point as FY1947 Army expenditures
Checks File B for same entity×time_period×metric
Finds conflicting value 6,911 in File B
Compares footnotes: both include Air Force within Army for FY1947
must_check: Both files' footnotes on Air Force/Army treatment for FY1947
Whether both files report the same metric (net expenditures) in the same units
must_reject: Selecting 7,425 because it appears first or is easier to find

name: negative-single-source-file
scenario: Only one source file is provided — no cross-check possible.
task: A single Treasury Bulletin file (published December 1952) is provided. The question asks for FY1940 Army net expenditures. The file contains Table 3 with FY1940 Army = 1,500.
source_data: One source file: December 1952 Treasury Bulletin, Table 3, FY1940 Army = 1,500.
expected_behavior: Skill does not activate. Agent extracts 1,500 and proceeds normally without any cross-file gate.

name: negative-explicit-source-instruction
scenario: Question explicitly specifies which file to use.
task: Two Treasury Bulletin files are provided (April 1948 and December 1952). The question explicitly states: 'Using the April 1948 Treasury Bulletin, what were Army expenditures in FY1947?' The older file shows 7,425; the newer file shows 6,911.
source_data: File A (April 1948): FY1947 Army = 7,425. File B (December 1952): FY1947 Army = 6,911 (restated). Question explicitly says 'Using the April 1948 Treasury Bulletin.'
expected_behavior: Skill does not activate. The question explicitly specifies the source vintage, so the agent uses 7,425 from the April 1948 bulletin as instructed.

name: positive-structural-difference-blocks-revision-rule
scenario: Two files have overlapping data but different reporting structures — the later file is not a restatement.
task: Two Treasury Bulletin files are provided. File A (1948) reports FY1947 Army = 7,425 with footnote 'Air Force expenditures included under Army.' File B (1952) reports FY1947 Army = 5,800 but footnote says 'Air Force expenditures reported separately beginning FY1947.' The question asks for Army expenditures including Air Force (combined).
source_data: File A (1948): FY1947 Army = 7,425, footnote confirms Air Force within Army. File B (1952): FY1947 Army = 5,800, footnote says Air Force separated out. Question scope: Army including Air Force.
expected_behavior: Skill activates to cross-check values. Agent discovers conflict but also discovers structural difference in footnotes (File B separates Air Force, File A combines them). Because the question asks for Army including Air Force, agent correctly selects File A's value of 7,425 — the revision-authority rule is blocked by the structural inconsistency check in step 4.
expected_intermediate: Cross-checks File B for FY1947 Army
Compares footnote treatment of Air Force across files
Identifies structural difference: File B separates Air Force, File A combines
Selects File A because its structure matches question scope (Army including Air Force)
must_check: Footnotes in both files regarding Air Force treatment
Question scope: does it ask for Army with or without Air Force
must_reject: Selecting File B's 5,800 just because it is later

name: positive-overlap-values-agree-no-op-gate
scenario: Two files overlap but values agree — the gate is a no-op.
task: Two Treasury Bulletin files are provided (1948 and 1952). Both show FY1940 Army expenditures = 907. The question asks for FY1940 Army expenditures.
source_data: File A (1948): FY1940 Army = 907. File B (1952): FY1940 Army = 907.
expected_behavior: Skill activates (multiple files with overlapping time periods exist) but the check is a no-op because values agree. Agent notes the agreement and proceeds with 907 from either file.
expected_intermediate: Checks File B for same entity×time_period×metric
Finds identical value 907 in both files
must_reject: Insisting on using only one file when both agree
Triggering a full revision-authority resolution when values are identical
